paper_metadata.title: Variational quantum eigensolver with linear depth problem-inspired ansatz for solving portfolio optimization in finance

experiments.description: Noise-free numerical simulation of portfolio optimization using the CCC ansatz versus CC and hardware-efficient (HE) ansatzes across varying asset counts, with fixed budget k=2 and varying CVaR confidence levels.

algorithm.variant: Variational quantum eigensolver with problem-inspired Dicke-state ansatz (CCC)

hyperparameters.samples_per_alpha: 1/alpha times the samples used for alpha=1

algorithm.parameter_initialization: random seed 1231 for parameters; asset pools initialized with 20 random seeds starting from 1000

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary asset-selection variable; Dicke-state subspace enforces fixed Hamming weight equal to budget
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x q x^T A x - mu^T x subject to budget constraint xi = 1^T x
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: hard constraint encoded in the ansatz subspace; CVaR used as local cost function
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Diagonal Hamiltonian corresponding to q' z^T A' z - mu'^T z after binary-to-spin transformation

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization with varying number of assets n in [4, 20], fixed budget k=2, and synthetic/market-derived asset data

dataset_specification.description: Asset data produced using qiskit_finance.data_providers; 20 random portfolio instances; no ticker symbols or date range reported

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20 independent asset-pool seeds; average time consumption, average optimal-solution probability, and average feasible-solution probability reported

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: linear in n; CCC depth of CNOTs is 2(n-k)
quantum_resources.num_shots: 1/alpha times the shots used for alpha=1

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Asset data generated with qiskit_finance.data_providers; parameters and asset pools initialized with fixed random seeds
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute average time, optimal probability, and feasible probability; feasible solution accepted when expectation is not more than 0.75 times the optimal expectation

speedup_claims.factor: linear-depth / O(nk) parameter scaling for CCC; lower than HE ansatz in practice
speedup_claims.conditions: noise-free simulations with fixed budget k=2 and CVaR cost
speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit asymptotic runtime speedup over classical optimization is demonstrated; comparison is only against other quantum ansatzes.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: CCC ansatz: O(nk) parameters and linear CNOT depth; for fixed k=2, depth and gate counts scale linearly with n

experiments.description: Noise-free numerical simulation of portfolio optimization using the CCC, CC, and HE ansatzes across varying budgets k for a fixed 12-asset instance.

algorithm.variant: Variational quantum eigensolver with problem-inspired Dicke-state ansatz (CCC and CC) compared against HE ansatz
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random seed 1231 for parameters; asset pools initialized with 20 random seeds starting from 1000

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary asset-selection variable; budget encoded by Dicke-state Hamming weight
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x q x^T A x - mu^T x subject to xi = 1^T x
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: hard constraint encoded in the ansatz subspace; CVaR cost function
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Diagonal Hamiltonian corresponding to q' z^T A' z - mu'^T z

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization with 12 assets and budgets k from 2 to 6

dataset_specification.description: 20 random portfolio instances; no ticker symbols or date range reported

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20 independent asset-pool seeds; average time consumption, average optimal-solution probability, and average feasible-solution probability reported

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: linear in n; CC and CCC ansatz depths depend on budget k

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Asset data generated with qiskit_finance.data_providers; fixed parameter seed and repeated asset-pool seeds
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Feasible solution defined by expectation not more than 0.75 times the optimal expectation

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline runtime or approximation guarantee is reported.

experiments.description: Noise-free numerical simulation comparing the effect of different asset orderings (original, reversed, shifted, random) on CCC and HE ansatz performance for a 12-asset portfolio with budget k=2.

algorithm.variant: Variational quantum eigensolver with asset-order sensitivity study
algorithm.parameter_initialization: parameters initialized once with random seed 1231; asset pool initialized once with seed 1000

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary variable; asset order changes the mapping of assets to qubits
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x q x^T A x - mu^T x subject to xi = 1^T x
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: hard constraint via Dicke-state ansatz; CVaR cost function
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Diagonal Hamiltonian corresponding to the portfolio objective

problem_instance.description: 12-asset portfolio optimization instance evaluated under four asset orderings

dataset_specification.description: Single asset pool instance with seed 1000; orderings tested: original, reversed, shift, random

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single initialization per ordering; compared time consumption, optimal probability, and feasible probability

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Asset ordering changed without reinitializing parameters; asset pool generated with seed 1000

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment studies sensitivity to asset ordering only; no classical baseline is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: linear-depth ansatz; performance depends on ordering due to restricted expressibility

experiments.description: Hardware experiment on a superconducting quantum computer implementing the HDC scheme for the k=3 CCC ansatz, partitioned into multiple 3-qubit fragments, with comparison to numerical simulation.

algorithm.variant: Quantum/classical hybrid distributed computing (HDC) with CCC ansatz, simultaneous sampling, measurement error mitigation, and fragment reuse
algorithm.convergence_criteria: not explicitly stated; iterative optimization with gradually increasing confidence level alpha
algorithm.parameter_initialization: uniform initialization of states for all subcircuits; confidence level alpha initially small and increased gradually to 1.0

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio optimization encoded via Dicke-state subspace with fixed Hamming weight k=3
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x q x^T A x - mu^T x subject to xi = 1^T x
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: hard constraint via ansatz; circuit cutting and measurement error mitigation used in HDC
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Diagonal portfolio Hamiltonian on the Dicke subspace

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization with k=3 on a superconducting quantum computer; up to 55 qubits used in the full distributed experiment

dataset_specification.description: Asset pool generated with random seed 1000; qubits 45, 46, 52 used in the reported hardware run

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Hardware versus simulation comparison; probability of obtaining the optimal solution reported

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: linear-depth staircase structure; each subcircuit uses multiple 3-qubit fragments
quantum_resources.num_shots: Table H1 lists shots in ICI as 8000, 4000, 2000, 2000, 1000, 1000, 3000 for different settings

noise_model.mitigation_details: Problem-specific measurement error mitigation using Hamming-weight-aware assignment matrix; simultaneous sampling; fragment reuse; confidence level alpha increased gradually
noise_model.noise_description: real hardware noise; measurement error mitigation applied

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Asset pool generated with seed 1000; subcircuits partitioned classically; uniform initialization of subcircuits
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Sequential sampling of fragments; measurement-error mitigation via inverse assignment matrix; normalization over correct Hamming-weight states

speedup_claims.factor: sampling complexity per subcircuit O(1/(alpha epsilon^2)); circuit submissions reduced to 2p+1
speedup_claims.conditions: HDC scheme with symmetry-aware measurement mitigation and simultaneous sampling
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims the sampling complexity is independent of total cut qubits p for these Dicke-state fragments; this is a methodological claim rather than a direct classical runtime comparison.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: HDC sampling complexity per subcircuit O(1/(alpha epsilon^2)); number of circuit submissions reduced to 2p+1 for p cut qubits

experiments.description: Hardware experiment on a superconducting quantum computer for the difficult |D12_6> portfolio instance using the HDC scheme with 6-qubit fragments and COBYLA optimization.

algorithm.variant: Quantum/classical hybrid distributed computing (HDC) with CCC ansatz for |D12_6>, fragment reuse, and measurement error mitigation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: iterative optimization over about 300 iterations shown in convergence plot; repeated primary-stage runs of COBYLA
algorithm.parameter_initialization: parameters randomly initialized in [pi/2, 3pi/4] and coarsely fitted to produce a relatively uniform output

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 12-asset portfolio with fixed Hamming weight k=6; 6 qubits per fragment
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x q x^T A x - mu^T x subject to xi = 1^T x
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: hard constraint via Dicke-state ansatz; HDC with fragment reuse and measurement error mitigation
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Portfolio Hamiltonian restricted to the Dicke subspace

dataset_specification.description: Asset pool generated with random seed 1000; coarse fitting used to initialize parameters

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Coarse fitting of parameters by minimizing deviation from uniform output probabilities
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Convergence curve reported; optimal-solution probability and CVaR expectation tracked over iterations

noise_model.mitigation_details: Measurement error mitigation; fragment reuse; repeated COBYLA primary-stage runs
noise_model.noise_description: real hardware noise; measurement error mitigation applied

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Coarse fitting of parameters to approximate uniform output; random initialization in [pi/2, 3pi/4]
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Repeated COBYLA runs with previous parameters used as next initial point; sequential fragment sampling and normalization

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline is reported; the experiment compares optimizer behavior on hardware and simulation only.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: HDC with 6-qubit fragments; sampling complexity per subcircuit O(1/(alpha epsilon^2))
